stories.headline: Anthropic Leak Reveals Claude Mythos, a 'Step Change' Model With Major Cybersecurity Capabilities

key_facts.fact: A CMS misconfiguration exposed draft blog posts about an unreleased model called Claude Mythos (also codenamed Capybara) in a publicly accessible data store.
key_facts.excerpt: A draft blog post and structured data for an unreleased AI model were discovered in an unsecured, publicly accessible data cache.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic confirmed the model is real, calling it 'the most capable we've built to date' and 'a step change' in AI performance.
key_facts.excerpt: An Anthropic spokesperson characterized it as representing 'a step change' in AI performance and 'the most capable we've built to date.'

key_facts.fact: Mythos is described as a new tier of model, larger and more intelligent than Opus, with 'dramatically higher scores' in coding, academic reasoning, and cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: Capybara gets dramatically higher scores on tests of software coding, academic reasoning, and cybersecurity, among others.

key_facts.fact: The leaked documents describe the model as 'currently far ahead of any other AI model in cyber capabilities,' warning it 'presages an upcoming wave of models that can exploit vulnerabilities in ways that far outpace the efforts of defenders.'
key_facts.excerpt: Currently far ahead of any other AI model in cyber capabilities... presages an upcoming wave of models that can exploit vulnerabilities in ways that far outpace the efforts of defenders.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic plans a phased rollout, starting with early access for organizations to evaluate cybersecurity applications before broader API availability.
key_facts.excerpt: Access begins with early-access customers focused on evaluating cybersecurity applications, then gradually expands through the Claude API.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic acknowledged the model is 'very expensive for us to serve, and will be very expensive for our customers to use' and plans optimization before broader release.
key_facts.excerpt: The company acknowledged the model is 'very expensive for us to serve, and will be very expensive for our customers to use' and plans optimization before broader release.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Codex Plugins With 20+ Integrations Including Slack, Figma, and Notion

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched plugins for Codex that integrate with Slack, Figma, Notion, Gmail, and Google Drive, bundling apps, prompt workflows ('skills'), and MCP server configurations into installable packages.
key_facts.excerpt: Plugins bundle three core components: 'predefined prompt workflows (skills), app integrations, and MCP server configurations' into installable packages.

key_facts.fact: Plugins extend Codex beyond coding to help with 'planning, research, and coordination,' working across the Codex app, command line, and IDE extensions.
key_facts.excerpt: The plugins extend beyond coding assistance. OpenAI states they 'help with planning, research, and coordination' alongside code-related tasks.

key_facts.fact: Codex has surpassed 1.6 million weekly active users, with plugins distributed through an official curated directory and developer self-publishing coming soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex has surpassed 1.6 million weekly active users, with a Windows version recently released following strong Mac adoption.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI simultaneously reset usage limits across all Codex plans, offering unlimited builds to coincide with the plugin launch.
key_facts.excerpt: We have reset Codex usage limits across all plans to let everyone experiment...You can just build unlimited things with Codex.

key_facts.fact: The launch is part of OpenAI's broader enterprise push, including plans to merge ChatGPT, Codex, and the Atlas browser into a unified desktop application.
key_facts.excerpt: This launch is part of OpenAI's broader enterprise push, including plans to merge ChatGPT, Codex, and the Atlas browser into a unified desktop application.

stories.headline: Anthropic Throttles Claude Session Limits During Peak Hours Amid Compute Strain

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is adjusting 5-hour session limits for Free, Pro ($20/mo), Max 5x ($100/mo), and Max 20x ($200/mo) tiers during peak hours (5am-11am PT / 1pm-7pm GMT on weekdays).
key_facts.excerpt: To manage the increasing demand for Claude, we're adjusting our five-hour session limits for free, Pro, and Max subscriptions during peak hours.

key_facts.fact: Approximately 7% of users will hit session limits they wouldn't have before, particularly Pro tier subscribers running token-intensive tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately 7% of users will encounter session limits they wouldn't have hit previously. Pro tier subscribers face the greatest likelihood of being affected.

key_facts.fact: Weekly usage limits remain unchanged; the change only affects how limits are distributed across the week, with session caps enforced based on token usage rather than clock time during peak hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Five-hour session limits now enforced based on token usage rather than clock time during peak hours. Weekly usage limits remain identical.

key_facts.fact: API customers are unaffected. Anthropic recommended users shift token-heavy background tasks to off-peak hours to reduce impact.
key_facts.excerpt: API customers are unaffected by these session limit changes. Users can shift token-heavy background tasks to off-peak hours to reduce impact.

stories.headline: Google's TurboQuant Algorithm Compresses AI Memory 6x, Wipes ~$100B From Memory Chip Stocks

key_facts.fact: Google Research published TurboQuant, a two-stage compression algorithm (PolarQuant + Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss) that reduces LLM inference KV cache memory by at least 6x with no accuracy loss.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant is a compression algorithm that reduces the memory footprint of large language models during inference... At least 6x smaller KV cache footprint.

key_facts.fact: The algorithm achieves 3-bit precision compression and up to 8x faster attention operations on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, requiring no model retraining.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to 8x faster attention operations on NVIDIA H100 GPU (4-bit vs. 32-bit). Down to 3-bit precision with no accuracy loss on tested benchmarks. No retraining required for existing models.

key_facts.fact: US memory chip stocks fell sharply: SanDisk (-6.5%), Seagate (-5%), Micron (-4%), Western Digital (-4%); in Asia, SK Hynix fell 4.42% and Samsung 3.02%.
key_facts.excerpt: SanDisk (-6.5%), Micron Technology (-4%), Western Digital (-4%), Seagate (-5%). SK Hynix (-4.42%), Samsung Electronics (-3.02%).

key_facts.fact: US memory chip stocks lost approximately $100 billion in market value during the week, led by Micron's 15% weekly drop.
key_facts.excerpt: US memory chip stocks lost ~$100B in market value this week, led by Micron's 15% drop, after Google Research detailed its TurboQuant compression algorithm.

key_facts.fact: The paper is slated for presentation at ICLR 2026. Analysts invoked the Jevons Paradox, suggesting efficiency gains could increase total AI memory demand through wider adoption.
key_facts.excerpt: Slated for presentation at ICLR 2026. Analysts invoked the 'Jevons Paradox' suggesting efficiency gains could actually increase total demand.

stories.headline: Mistral Launches Voxtral: Open-Weights ASR Beating Whisper and 4B-Parameter TTS With Voice Cloning

key_facts.fact: Mistral released Voxtral in two ASR sizes: Voxtral 24B (built on Mistral Small 3.1) and Voxtral Mini 3B (built on Ministral 3B for edge), plus a 4B-parameter TTS model, all supporting 9 languages.
key_facts.excerpt: Voxtral 24B: Built on Mistral Small 3.1 backbone. Voxtral Mini 3B: Built on Ministral 3B for edge deployments. TTS Model: 4 billion parameters. Nine languages with automatic detection.

key_facts.fact: Voxtral 24B achieved 'best in class' performance against Whisper large-v3, GPT-4o mini Transcribe, and Gemini 2.5 Flash on English short-form and FLEURS multilingual benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Voxtral 24B achieved 'best in class' performance against Whisper large-v3, GPT-4o mini Transcribe, and Gemini 2.5 Flash on English short-form and FLEURS multilingual benchmarks.

key_facts.fact: The TTS model can clone a voice from as little as 3 seconds of reference audio, with API latency of 70ms to first audio at $0.016 per 1,000 characters.
key_facts.excerpt: Can clone a custom voice from as little as three seconds of reference audio, capturing accent, inflection, and natural speech patterns. TTS API: $0.016 per 1,000 characters with 70ms latency.

key_facts.fact: ASR models are released under Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face; TTS is CC BY NC 4.0 (commercial use requires separate agreement). ASR API is priced at $0.001 per minute.
key_facts.excerpt: ASR: Apache 2.0 license, downloadable on Hugging Face. TTS: CC BY NC 4.0 (commercial use requires separate agreement). ASR API: $0.001 per minute.

stories.headline: NeurIPS Reverses Sanctions Ban on Chinese Researchers After Boycott Threat From CCF and CAST

key_facts.fact: On March 23, NeurIPS updated its handbook to ban submissions, peer review, and publication from anyone linked to US-sanctioned organizations including Huawei, SMIC, and SenseTime.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 23, 2026, NeurIPS updated its handbook requiring compliance with US sanctions laws, stating that 'no services — including paper submissions, peer review, or publication' would be available to anyone linked to sanctioned organizations.

key_facts.fact: China Computer Federation (CCF) urged all Chinese researchers to boycott NeurIPS, and China Association for Science and Technology (CAST) halted funding and said NeurIPS papers would no longer count toward academic evaluations in China.
key_facts.excerpt: CCF urged all Chinese researchers to boycott NeurIPS. CAST halted funding for researchers attending the 2026 event and announced NeurIPS papers would no longer count toward academic evaluations or promotions in China.

key_facts.fact: On March 27, NeurIPS reversed the policy and apologized, admitting it had 'gone beyond legal requirements' and the handbook 'pointed to a broad US sanctions tool that covered more restrictions than actually needed.'
key_facts.excerpt: NeurIPS issued an apology, admitting they had 'gone beyond legal requirements' and that the handbook 'pointed to a broad US sanctions tool that covered more restrictions than actually needed.'

key_facts.fact: The corrected policy now applies only to entities on the US Treasury's SDN (Specially Designated Nationals) list rather than the broader sanctions list.
key_facts.excerpt: The policy was a mistake due to a miscommunication with their legal team and clarified that it applies only to entities on the U.S. Treasury's SDN list.

stories.headline: Google's Internal 'Agent Smith' AI Coding Tool Became So Popular It Had to Be Restricted

key_facts.fact: Google has deployed an internal AI tool called 'Agent Smith' that autonomously handles coding and workflow tasks in the background, even without an active laptop.
key_facts.excerpt: Google employees have flocked to a new internal AI tool called 'Agent Smith' that can autonomously handle coding and workflow tasks in the background — even without an active laptop.

key_facts.fact: Employees can monitor and guide Agent Smith from their mobile phones, enabling asynchronous coding where the AI works while engineers are away.
key_facts.excerpt: The system can operate asynchronously, completing work in the background while employees monitor or guide it via mobile devices.

key_facts.fact: The tool became so popular internally that Google had to restrict access due to overwhelming usage, according to three people familiar with the tool.

stories.headline: Microsoft Leases Crusoe's 900MW Abilene Data Center After Oracle and OpenAI Withdrew

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will lease Crusoe Energy's 900MW data center project in Abilene, Texas, after Oracle and OpenAI reportedly withdrew from the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft rents data center project developed for Oracle, OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: The first building is expected to be operational by mid-2027. Microsoft's Noelle Walsh, President of Cloud Operations & Innovation, said the company is 'focused on ensuring access to reliable and responsible infrastructure at scale.'
key_facts.excerpt: As customer demand for AI continues to grow, Microsoft is focused on ensuring access to reliable and responsible infrastructure at scale.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft CEO Mustafa Suleyman called it a 'great way to wrap up the week,' describing it as a '900MW AI factory' to add capacity to Microsoft's AI fleet.
